title: Chapter 102
content:
Young Il-hyun floated on a yellow swim tube, splashing his feet in the private pool.

Mom. Look at me, Mom.

He called out to the woman lounging on the patio lounger, crying for her over and over. But she simply swallowed another glass of dark red wine, never sparing him a single glance.

Desperate to catch her eye, he lifted both hands to wave. The sudden shift in weight tipped the tube, dumping his small frame straight under.

The cold water closed over his head, choking the air from his small lungs as he flailed his arms.

Help... Help me! Mom! Please help me! Mom!

Through the churning foam, she finally turned her head.

Holding her wine glass by the stem, her dark eyes peered down into the water—silent, hollow, and utterly still. She looked like someone patiently waiting for a dying animal to stop breathing.

Water flooded down his throat, burning his chest as his strength drained away. His small body sank deeper into the cold blue depths.

It was strange. He shouldn't be able to breathe underwater, yet his lungs dragged in air with impossible ease.

Worse, he wasn't alone.

Drifting in the shadows beneath the surface were dozens of faces staring at him with unadulterated venom. People with severed heads, missing fingers, and gouged throats floated together in the dark abyss, surrounding his sinking body. The bright sunlight filtering through the surface grew distant and faint.

The slaughtered corpses began drifting closer, reaching out with cold, pale hands. Terrified, young Il-hyun shrieked, thrashing against the dead.

Suddenly, a figure cut through the surface.

Diving through the churning water with powerful, fluid strokes, someone descended into the deep, extending a hand without a trace of hesitation.

The instant Il-hyun seized that warm palm to save his life, his eyes flew wide open.

A sterile white ceiling drifted into focus through a heavy blur. He rolled his eyes left and right. Intravenous lines hung suspended from steel tracks overhead, accompanied by the steady, rhythmic beeping of cardiac monitors. He flexed his fingertips and toes.

A nurse stepped through the door, pausing mid-stride with wide eyes. She rushed out, and moments later a team of physicians crowded around the bed.

A sharp penlight flared across his pupils. As his vision cleared, he spotted Dr. Kang Yu-jung standing among the white coats.

Il-hyun? Are you with us? Can you hear my voice?

He tried to answer, but the clear plastic oxygen mask clamped over his mouth muffled the sound into a dry rasp. When he blinked twice in response, a look of immense relief washed over Yu-jung's face, her lips pressing into a trembling line as she bit back a sob.
Returning to the mountain estate after ten days in the hospital, Jakyeong found the grounds entirely unchanged. The villa remained wrapped in quiet luxury, and the regular security rotation patrolled the perimeter as if nothing had happened.

Jakyeong chose not to stay in his second-floor guest suite; instead, he settled into Kang Il-hyun’s master bedroom on the ground floor. Curling up on the mattress that still held the man's familiar cedar aftershave, he buried his face in Il-hyun's pillow, pulling the heavy duvet tight around his shoulders.

The steady tick of the wall clock felt overwhelmingly loud in the dark. Several times throughout the night, he checked his phone for updates from the hospital wing.

Whenever he rolled over, the king-sized mattress felt cavernous and cold. Without its master, the room held zero warmth.

He drifted into a shallow sleep, only for nightmares to drag him under. He dreamed that he and Il-hyun were out together, only for the man to vanish into thin air. No matter how loudly Jakyeong screamed his name, searching every corner of the earth, Il-hyun never reappeared. Even within the dream, the sheer terror crushed the breath from his chest.

He woke with a start, unable to fall back asleep.

Waiting for dawn felt excruciating. When the first pale light broke over the tree line, his very first reflex was to check for missed calls. Finding zero notifications brought a pang of bitter disappointment, yet knowing no disastrous news had arrived provided a quiet sigh of relief.

In the master bath, he washed his face carefully, keeping water clear of the fresh stitches along his arms. Stepping into the kitchen, his face was swollen and drawn from sleep deprivation.

The senior housekeeper looked at him with gentle, aching concern. "Are you holding up, Young Master?"

"Yes..." He gave a small nod.

Over the past few days, everyone seemed to ask if he was alright. He kept claiming he was fine, but nothing felt further from the truth. A phantom ache throbbed in his chest as if half his heart had been carved out with a knife. Eating, sitting, breathing—every stray second dragged his thoughts right back to Kang Il-hyun until it became unbearable.

What if the man took a turn for the worse while Jakyeong was resting here? Standing vigil at the hospital didn't magically improve his recovery, but the gnawing anxiety made it impossible to focus on anything else.

Telling the housekeeper he would skip breakfast, he pulled on a jacket, snatched the sedan keys from the console, and headed for the front door.

She caught him by the sleeve. "Where are you going in such a rush?"

"The hospital..."

Her gaze drifted down to his left leg. Jakyeong quickly insisted the hairline fracture was minor and wouldn't interfere with driving an automatic. She let out a soft sigh, attempting to summon a chauffeur, but Jakyeong deflected her concerns and slipped out to the garage.

Twenty minutes down the highway, Wang Han rang his phone. Over the receiver, his handler shouted in pure fury, but Jakyeong calmly assured him he would return shortly, enduring threats that he’d be tied to his bedpost tomorrow.

Reaching the hospital grounds, he parked in the quiet morning lot and limped across the lobby. Moving by pure muscle memory, he took his usual seat on the hard plastic bench outside the intensive care unit, bracing for another grueling wait.

A familiar floor nurse stepped through the double doors, stopping dead in her tracks with round eyes.

"Goodness... weren't you discharged just yesterday?"

Jakyeong managed an awkward, sheepish grimace.

"You arrived at the perfect time."

"Pardon?"

"Director Kang regained consciousness before dawn. He was transferred to a private recovery suite an hour ago."

The news hit him like a shockwave. Jakyeong sprang up from the bench with a breathless gasp. "Is that true?"

She nodded with a warm, confirming smile.

Jakyeong’s face lit up with a brilliant, unrestrained grin. Muttering several breathless thank-yous, he scrambled toward the elevators.

Locating the suite was effortless. A detail of suited security operatives stood in silent formation outside the VIP corner room. Spotting Jakyeong, they bowed respectfully.

Mounted beside the heavy wooden door was a sleek brass plaque bearing three familiar characters: Kang Il-hyun.

He truly woke up. His heart hammered against his ribs, an overwhelming surge of emotion choking his throat.

He raised a trembling hand to knock, but hesitated at the threshold, drawing a deep breath to steady his racing pulse. Before his knuckles could graze the wood, the door clicked open, and a team of physicians filed out in single file.

Among them was Kang Yu-jung.

She did a double-take upon spotting Jakyeong, her own face noticeably brighter than the days before. She asked how he’d found out so quickly, given she hadn't even briefed Park Tae-soo yet.

The door drifted shut behind her, obscuring the view inside. Sensing his frantic impatience, a teasing smile touched her lips.

"He really... opened his eyes?" Jakyeong stammered.

Her expression shifted into mock reluctance. "He did. Though I'm not entirely sure you should go in right this second."

"Why... what happened?"

"I told him you packed your bags and ran off."

Yu-jung gave an amused chuckle, adjusting her lab coat. "If he starts shouting the moment you walk in, I'm claiming total ignorance."

With a wink, she followed the medical team down the hall.

Jakyeong stood blinking in bewilderment. Why on earth would she tell him that...?

He turned the handle and pushed the door open.

Propped up against the pillows in the center of the spacious room, Kang Il-hyun was glaring at the doorway with a scowl fierce enough to curdle milk.

He's truly awake.

Seeing the man breathing on his own sent a sudden, hot sting rushing to Jakyeong’s eyes. Mortified at the thought of crying in front of him, Jakyeong whipped around, facing the hallway wall.

I might not believe in higher powers, but thank you, God. Thank you, Buddha. Thank you for keeping him alive. I'll live the rest of my life doing good deeds.

As he fought to swallow the lump in his throat, a dry, incredulous chuckle rumbled from the bed.

"Look who decided to show up. And here I was, working myself into a pure rage thinking you'd run off again."

"..."

"Why are you standing there with your back to me?"

"..."

When Jakyeong refused to turn around, the mocking edge in Il-hyun's voice vanished.

"Lee Ja-kyeong."

Hearing his true name spoken in that familiar, rough baritone shattered the last remnants of Jakyeong’s composure.

Fat, heavy tears spilled over his lashes, dripping steadily onto the linoleum floor.

Piecing the silence together, Il-hyun’s tone softened into a quiet, tender purr.

"Are you... crying?"

"No... I'm not," Jakyeong choked out, the words dissolving into a wet, breathless hiccup.

"Come here. Let me see your face."

Reluctantly, Jakyeong turned back around, wiping his cheek with his sleeve.

Il-hyun’s dark eyes narrowed as he took in the sight. Jakyeong’s nose and eyelids were flushed a vivid, swollen crimson from weeping—looking so thoroughly wrecked and precious it made Il-hyun’s chest tighten.

Il-hyun gritted his teeth, fighting back the sudden, inappropriate surge of lust flaring in his gut.

Fuck me. I just crawled out of the grave, and the first thing I want to do is pin him down and take him apart.

I should have taken a photo of this. Regretting that his phone was nowhere in sight, Il-hyun crooked a finger, gesturing for him to approach.

Then, his eyes caught the uneven limp in Jakyeong’s gait. The teasing warmth on his face instantly hardened into stone.

"What happened to your leg?"

"It's nothing serious. Just a hairline fracture."

"How did that happen?"

The memory of falling from the concrete ledge flared up, making Jakyeong’s voice crack with indignant rage.

"Because you pushed me off the damn building, you bastard!"

Who asked you to save me? Who told you to trade your life for mine? Who asked you to die in my place?!

The overwhelming guilt, anger, and relief that had been festering for days broke through all at once. As Jakyeong scrubbed furiously at his wet face with his bandaged forearm, Il-hyun pulled several tissues from the nightstand, patting the edge of the mattress.

"Sit down."

The moment Jakyeong sank onto the bed, Il-hyun reached out, carefully dabbing the tears from his cheeks before cupping his jaw with a warm, steady palm. A kaleidoscope of raw emotions flickered across Il-hyun's dark pupils.

"Seeing you weep like this over me... I suppose I don't have to worry about you running away anymore."

Even battered and bandaged, the man completely ignored his own life-threatening wounds, scanning Jakyeong from head to toe to inspect every scratch. The sheer, maddening tenderness only made Jakyeong cry harder, tears streaming down his face in pure frustration.

Fuck. This is humiliating. If the Wang brothers ever saw this, they’d hold it over my head until the day I die.

When the sobbing finally subsided into quiet sniffles, Il-hyun extended his arms.

"Done crying? Come here. I want to hold you."

Mindful of the surgical dressings wrapping the man's chest, Jakyeong leaned in with extreme care, wrapping his arms around Il-hyun's broad shoulders.

A low, vibrating chuckle rumbled right against Jakyeong’s ear.

The mocking bravado from before had faded entirely, leaving Il-hyun’s voice thick with raw, trembling moisture.

"Coming back from the dead... isn't so bad after all."
